overview:
Dynamic Updates are how Palo Alto keeps your firewall's brain current without requiring a full PAN-OS upgrade. Think of it as the firewall's subscription to staying relevant — Palo Alto frequently publishes updates the firewall can use to enforce security policy, without requiring you to change the firewall configuration or upgrade software.

There are a few different update types and it's worth knowing what each one does:

Applications and Threats — keeps App-ID and threat signatures current. This is the big one.
Antivirus — updates anti-virus and anti-spyware signatures
WildFire — near real-time malware intelligence from Palo Alto's cloud sandbox
GlobalProtect — data files for the VPN client

Which updates are available to you depends on your subscriptions — so if you don't have a Threat Prevention license, you won't see everything.
WildFire can be set to update as frequently as every 15 minutes, while Applications and Threats can be scheduled hourly, daily, or weekly, and Antivirus can run hourly, daily, or weekly. In my environment I run Applications and Threats daily and WildFire every 15 minutes — find what makes sense for yours.
One thing worth knowing: always update content before updating PAN-OS. Every PAN-OS version has a minimum supported content version, so don't skip this step when you're prepping for a software upgrade.

# Retrieve Dynamic Updates
<mark style="background: #ABF7F7A6;">Operational mode ></mark>

## Applications and Threats
```
request content upgrade check
```
```
request content upgrade download latest
```
```
request content upgrade install version latest
```
## Antivirus
```
request anti-virus upgrade check
```
```
request anti-virus upgrade download latest
```
```
request anti-virus upgrade install version latest
```
## Wildfire
```
request wildfire upgrade check
```
```
request wildfire upgrade download latest
```
```
request wildfire upgrade install version latest
```


# Check for Available PAN-OS Software Versions
<mark style="background: #ABF7F7A6;">Operational mode ></mark>
```
request system software check
```
```
request system software download version <version_number>
```
```
request system software install version <version_number>
```
```
request restart system
```
